rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This tests the simplest configuration (rna_only with singleprofile and PCA encoder) to compare against more complex models. It isolates the effect of modality and encoder choice, providing a reference point for evaluating subsequent configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile (profile_setting=multiprofile) with avgpool aggregation improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile aggregation) while building on the baseline RNA-only setting, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.5907 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile (config_001, 0.4849). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) in the multiprofile setup improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. This addresses a key design decision (encoder type) while maintaining the promising multiprofile/avgpool combination, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005, 0.65 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and PCA-based models. This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to the best RNA-only setup, using avgpool (proven effective in config_002/005) and concat fusion. It isolates the impact of multimodal integration while building on established effective components, balancing exploitation of known strengths with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool (used in config_005) to transformer (config_006) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This clarifies whether advanced aggregation techniques benefit the strong scvi_n200 RNA encoder, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing RNA-only model with exploration of critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that for rna_only, using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation (config_006) achieves the highest accuracy (0.6529). This experiment tests whether combining this effective RNA encoder and aggregation method with image data (resnet50) in a multimodal setting improves performance. It isolates the impact of adding image modality while keeping RNA and aggregation strategies proven in prior experiments, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (config_032) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method to weighted improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion type. This is a logical extension of the current best and helps determine the importance of fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with a larger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) further improves performance, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. It is the best next step as it explores a critical design decision (image encoder) in the top-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of potential improvements.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder while maintaining the same image encoder, fusion method, and aggregation (avgpool) isolates the impact of the RNA encoder. It reduces uncertainty about whether scgpt could further improve performance, while keeping other variables consistent.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve high accuracy (0.7249). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (config_050) affects performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. This is critical to determine if weighted fusion is essential for the observed performance, balancing exploration of key design choices while building on a promising direction.
